root_cause.text: In the MPTCP in-kernel path `mptcp_pm_create_subflow_or_signal_addr()`, endpoints configured with both `signal` and `subflow` could send an ADD_ADDR without ever incrementing `msk->pm.local_addr_used` when subflow creation was blocked, leaving the endpoint marked used in `id_avail_bitmap` but not in the local-usage counter and triggering the later WARN on removal in `__mark_subflow_endp_available()`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE says the bug happens when subflows are limited to 0, an endpoint has both `signal` and `subflow`, an ADD_ADDR is sent, and then removing the endpoint warns because `msk->pm.local_addr_used` stayed 0 even though the bitmap bit was cleared; the patch fixes this by adding `if (signal_and_subflow && local.addr.id != msk->mpc_endpoint_id) msk->pm.local_addr_used++;` with the comment that subflow-capable endpoints must still be “marked as used” when no subflow could be created.

intent_record.intent_summary: Ensure dual-purpose endpoints are marked used even when subflow creation fails, preventing later endpoint removal accounting issues.
intent_record.what: A new conditional block was added at the exit of mptcp_pm_create_subflow_or_signal_addr() that increments msk->pm.local_addr_used when signal_and_subflow is true and no subflow was created (local.addr.id != msk->mpc_endpoint_id). A comment was also added explaining that this marks the endpoint as used so later endpoint removal logic can rely on the increment.
intent_record.how: At runtime, endpoints configured for both signaling and subflow use will now still be counted as used even if subflow creation could not happen. This prevents later cleanup/removal code from seeing an unexpectedly unmarked endpoint and avoids inconsistencies in __mark_subflow_endp_available() accounting.
